raw_response:
I've been working this land for thirty years, and my father worked it before me. I know what Quzhou soil needs. I don't read books or go to training sessions, but I know what my neighbors do and what has worked harvest after harvest.

My whole 10.1 mu rotates between wheat and maize — same land, both seasons. That's how everyone here does it. Wheat goes in October, comes out June. Maize straight after, out by late September. No rest for the land, no rest for me.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll use Jimai 22. Everyone around here uses it, it's reliable and the seed seller I've bought from for fifteen years stocks it. I'll rotary till after the maize comes off — quick and easy. I put down base fertilizer when I plant: compound fertilizer plus urea. Then I top-dress at jointing. I always do four irrigations — sowing water to get germination, winter water before the freeze, jointing water, and heading water. Maybe a fifth if it's dry at grain fill. I spray herbicide in winter when weeds come up, then a fungicide-insecticide mix around heading to stop rust and aphids. That's three spray trips.

**Maize (summer):** I buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — it yields well and I can get it locally. After wheat harvest I do a quick rotary pass, then plant within a few days so I don't lose soil moisture. I throw on compound fertilizer at planting and chase it with urea at the big bell stage. Two or three irrigations depending on what the sky gives me — usually one right after planting if it's dry, one at tasseling. Spray herbicide right after emergence, then check for corn borer mid-season and spray if I see it. Two pesticide trips usually.

I won't change much this year. Prices for inputs are up but so is grain price. I'll hold my fertilizer rates steady — I know some younger farmers cut back and their yields suffered.
